standard_title: ESSCA II Attachment J-21 — Task Order and Delivery Order Content Requirements

part_index.title: Task Order Request Content — TO Level
Task Order Request Content — Sub-Task Level

1.statement_text: A Task Order (TO) is created through a two-step process: (1) The Government creates a Task Order Request (TOR) which is reviewed within the Government, then routed to the Contractor following approval by the contracting officer (CO). (2) The Contractor creates a Task Order Plan (TOP) which is returned to the Government for internal review. Once the CO approves the TOP, the joint content of the TOR and corresponding TOP constitute the TO.
1.subject: Task Order creation
1.requirement: Two-step process with CO approval at both steps (TOR approval and TOP approval) before a TO is constituted

1.statement_text: The Government creates a Task Order Request (TOR) which is reviewed within the Government, then routed to the Contractor following approval by the contracting officer (CO).
1.subject: TOR routing
1.requirement: TOR must be approved by CO before routing to Contractor

1.statement_text: Once the CO approves the TOP, the joint content of the TOR and corresponding TOP constitute the TO.
1.subject: TO constitution
1.requirement: CO must approve TOP; only the joint TOR+TOP content constitutes the binding TO

1.statement_text: Revision Number (auto-increment with each TO change request [TOCR])
1.subject: Revision tracking
1.requirement: Every TOCR must increment the revision number; changes are tracked through the TOCR mechanism

2.subject: TO-level content
2.requirement: Every TO must include Description/Objectives at the TO level

2.statement_text: Summary of changes (specific to a TOCR, the summary must include the CWBS, sections changed, description of change, and cost impact. The description may be divided into separate Government and Contractor fields)
2.subject: Summary of Changes
2.requirement: Every TOCR Summary of Changes MUST include four mandatory fields: (1) CWBS, (2) sections changed, (3) description of change, (4) cost impact

2.statement_text: CWBS: Performing Organization, Skill, and Task ID (PSID) (Partially completed by d & e, refer to Attachment J-9, Contract Work Breakdown Structure for numbering information)
2.subject: CWBS
2.requirement: Every TO must have a CWBS with Performing Organization, Skill, and Task ID (PSID)

2.subject: Period of performance
2.requirement: Every TO must specify period of performance with start and end dates

2.statement_text: Urgency (Normal/Emergency) as a roll-up of sub-task urgency designations
2.subject: Urgency designation
2.requirement: TO-level urgency must be designated and must roll up from sub-task urgency levels

2.subject: Technical direction justification
2.requirement: TO must include justification for technical direction

2.statement_text: Skill (selectable entry used to partially fill in the CWBS)
2.subject: Skill designation
2.requirement: TO must designate a Skill from the ATOMS selectable entries; this Skill partially populates the CWBS and defines the authorized work domain

2.subject: TO title
2.requirement: Every TO must have a title

2.statement_text: Task Initiator (TI) (may be selectable-entry based on active TI accounts)
2.subject: Task Initiator
2.requirement: Every TO must identify a Task Initiator

2.statement_text: Performing Organization (selectable-entry used to partially fill in the CWBS)
2.subject: Performing Organization
2.requirement: Every TO must identify the Performing Organization

2.subject: Review comments
2.requirement: TO must include a review comments field

3.subject: Sub-task structure
3.requirement: Each sub-task must have a title

3.statement_text: CWBS, to include: PSID, funding source, funding sub-source, and activity (selectable for each CWBS level or entered manually)
3.subject: Sub-task CWBS and funding
3.requirement: Each sub-task MUST have a CWBS entry with PSID, funding source, funding sub-source, and activity. Work without a CWBS and funding source cannot be authorized.

3.subject: Sub-task period of performance
3.requirement: Each sub-task must specify period of performance

3.statement_text: Urgency (Normal/Emergency) (Yes/No) as referenced in NFS 1852.216-80, Task Ordering Procedure.
3.subject: Sub-task urgency
3.requirement: Each sub-task must designate urgency per NFS 1852.216-80

3.subject: Sub-task description
3.requirement: Each sub-task must have its own Description/Objectives defining the scope of work for that sub-task

3.subject: Sub-task skills
3.requirement: Each sub-task must specify the skills required for the work

3.subject: Sub-task deliverables
3.requirement: Each sub-task must define deliverables, milestones, travel requirements, and risk

3.statement_text: Resource Analyst (RA)(may be selectable-entry based on active RA account)
3.subject: Resource Analyst assignment
3.requirement: Each sub-task must have an assigned Resource Analyst

3.subject: Emergency justification
3.requirement: Emergency sub-tasks must include justification for emergency authorization

3.statement_text: Place of performance for the work (if not onsite)
3.subject: Place of performance
3.requirement: Non-onsite work must specify place of performance

3.statement_text: Select whether the TO is severable or non-severable, and include a rationale box for non-severable designations
3.subject: Severability designation
3.requirement: TO must designate severable/non-severable with rationale for non-severable

3.statement_text: Government-Furnished Equipment (GFE), Materials, Supplies, and Equipment
3.subject: GFE identification
3.requirement: Sub-task must identify any required GFE, materials, supplies, and equipment

4.subject: Contractor data — TO Manager
4.requirement: Contractor must designate TO Manager(s) in the TOP

4.subject: Contractor data — Summary of Changes
4.requirement: Contractor-supplied TOP must include Summary of Changes

4.statement_text: Discussion of Skills required (labor skill mix)
4.subject: Contractor data — Skills discussion
4.requirement: TOP must include discussion of skills required with labor skill mix

4.statement_text: Participating Team (including subcontractors), by Company name
4.subject: Contractor data — Team
4.requirement: TOP must identify participating team including subcontractors by company name

4.statement_text: Materials, supplies, tools, facilities, and equipment required and whether such items will be Government provided, Contractor provided, or acquired by the Contractor as part of the TO Other Direct Costs (ODC). This includes any anticipated purchases that are over $250,000 (including estimated acquisition cost)
4.subject: Contractor data — Materials and ODC
4.requirement: TOP must identify all materials/supplies/equipment, their source (Government/Contractor/ODC), and any purchases over $250K

4.statement_text: Include a plan of costs for the proposed task order that shows the (i) changes and (ii) resulting costs, phased by month by the various cost categories (e.g., Labor, materials, Equipment, Travel, Training, Relocation) including both labor hours (decomposed into the component labor categories, and distinguishing any direct-charged management labor from other labor) and work year equivalents (WYE's).
4.subject: Contractor data — Cost plan
4.requirement: TOP MUST include a cost plan showing: (1) changes, (2) resulting costs phased by month, (3) breakdown by cost category, (4) labor hours decomposed by labor category, (5) direct-charged management labor distinguished from other labor, (6) work year equivalents

4.statement_text: Deliverables and Milestones (including subcontractor deliverables and any lower-level deliverables developed by the Contractor)
4.subject: Contractor data — Deliverables
4.requirement: TOP must specify all deliverables and milestones, including subcontractor deliverables

4.statement_text: Delivery/Performance Schedule, including start and end dates
4.subject: Contractor data — Schedule
4.requirement: TOP must include delivery/performance schedule with start and end dates

4.statement_text: Risk Assessment and Risk Mitigation Plan
4.subject: Contractor data — Risk
4.requirement: TOP must include risk assessment and risk mitigation plan

4.statement_text: Cost Estimate to include labor categories and labor hours segregated for Prime and subcontractors, and travel, training, ODCs, and material
4.subject: Contractor data — Cost estimate
4.requirement: TOP must include cost estimate with labor hours segregated by Prime and subcontractor

4.statement_text: Maximum estimated cost and fee, and fee period allocations
4.subject: Contractor data — Cost ceiling
4.requirement: TOP must include maximum estimated cost, fee, and fee period allocations

4.statement_text: Organizational Conflict of Interest (OCI) Notification (if needed)
4.subject: Contractor data — OCI
4.requirement: TOP must include OCI notification when applicable

4.statement_text: Special considerations (e.g., recruiting, consulting, safety concerns) that may affect performance
4.subject: Contractor data — Special considerations
4.requirement: TOP must identify special considerations affecting performance

5.statement_text: Task Order/Delivery Order Creation and Change Process: TI Submits TOR/TOCR → TM Review/Approve → RA Review/Approve → COR Review/Approve → CO Review/Approve → CO Issues (revised) TO/DO. All paths terminate at CO approval.
5.subject: Approval chain
5.requirement: Every TO creation or change must traverse the full approval chain: Task Initiator → Technical Monitor → Resource Analyst → COR → CO. No step may be bypassed. CO approval is the terminal gate.

5.statement_text: Scope or POP change with cost impact triggers the standard TOCR flow (not Technical Direction flow)
5.subject: Scope change routing
5.requirement: Any change involving scope or period of performance with cost impact must follow the TOCR flow, not the Technical Direction flow

5.statement_text: Emergency Authorization TOs only: Emergency TOR/TOCR flow requires TI submit → TM Review → COR Review → CO Review/Approve → Contractor discussions with CO and COR
5.subject: Emergency flow
5.requirement: Even emergency TOCRs require TM, COR, and CO review/approval. Emergency status does not eliminate approval requirements.

5.statement_text: TOP/TOCP Prepared, Submitted by Contractor → Return to Contractor for Rework if rejected → COR Review/Approve → CO Review/Approve → CO Issues (revised) TO/DO
5.subject: Contractor submission and review
5.requirement: Contractor prepares and submits TOP/TOCP; if rejected at any review stage, returned to Contractor for rework. Final issuance is by CO only.

5.statement_text: No path in the TO/DO creation and change process permits a contractor team lead to independently modify, approve, or issue a task order or task order revision without traversing the full TI → TM → RA → COR → CO approval chain.
5.subject: Prohibition on bypassing approval chain
5.requirement: Contractor personnel below the designated roles (TI, TM, RA, COR, CO) may not modify or approve task order scope. A team lead is not a designated approval authority in the J-21 process flow.

5.statement_text: TOR/TOCR/DOR/DOCR submitted by TI. Return to Initiator if not resolved at any review stage.
5.subject: Initiator responsibility
5.requirement: All TORs and TOCRs must be submitted by the designated Task Initiator. Unresolved issues are returned to the initiator.

5.statement_text: Combined requirement: Every task order change request (TOCR) must (1) include a Summary of Changes with CWBS, sections changed, description, and cost impact [§1.1(k)], AND (2) traverse the full approval chain TI → TM → RA → COR → CO [Fig J-21-1], AND (3) increment the revision number [§1.1(b)]. A scope change that bypasses any of these three requirements violates J-21.
5.subject: Combined TOCR compliance rule
5.requirement: Three simultaneous requirements for any TOCR: mandatory Summary of Changes fields, mandatory approval chain, and mandatory revision increment. Failure on any one is a J-21 violation.
